06db3b6cbc.q: How did Chad Babcock start the Tumble Bus business and scale it to four buses within two years?
06db3b6cbc.a: Chad Babcock received a $10,000 loan from his grandfather, bought a $5,000 school bus, gutted it out himself, painted it with 'Magic Tumble Bus' in colorful letters, and went door-to-door to childcares and preschool centers introducing himself. Within two years, he had four buses operating with employees, learning payroll and business operations by doing it.

8f3c43886d.q: What was Chad Babcock's journey from opening his first trampoline park in 2010 to operating multiple locations?
8f3c43886d.a: In 2009, Chad Babcock discovered Jump Street facility in Colorado and decided to build Idaho's first trampoline park in 2010, making it the 25th park in the world. He hired a general manager to run it from afar rather than working there directly. He subsequently built additional parks in Boise (10 miles away, leased), Twin Falls Idaho (40,000 square feet, purchased building), Meridian (36,000 square feet, purchased property), and Bozeman Montana, eventually consolidating to three trampoline parks still operating today.

cf4d293b25.q: What key advice does Chad Babcock offer entrepreneurs about building a business with an exit strategy in mind?
cf4d293b25.a: Chad Babcock stresses that entrepreneurs should build their business with the intention of selling it, preparing for a sale even if it is 10 years down the road. He explains that preparing to sell while building makes the eventual sale process much easier and prevents discovering too late all the things one should have done differently.

f61f2a048e.q: How did Chad Babcock transition from teaching gymnastics to building a full-scale gymnastics gym and preschool facility?
f61f2a048e.a: While running the Tumble Bus program, a client named Brenda from Kangaroo Pocket told Chad about a closed chiropractor gym (1,800 square feet) with $40,000 of equipment. Chad took over the lease for six months at $1,200 per month, intending to use it for equipment storage. His wife quit her teaching job to call contacts, and they signed up 60 students in the first week. Within two years, the facility doubled in size, and they built a 12,800 square foot building combining gymnastics and preschool.

d17a948c82.q: What support systems has Chad Babcock used to sustain entrepreneurial growth, particularly the Entrepreneurs Organization?
d17a948c82.a: About 15 years ago, Chad Babcock joined Entrepreneurs Organization (EO), a group of seven members that eventually split off to run independently as a forum meeting monthly. His group comprises people from different industries (IT supplements, prosthetics, AI) but facing similar entrepreneurial challenges. They discuss businesses, successes, challenges, and share personal and emotional support, all kept confidential, providing strategic learning and idea-sharing beyond his own business sector.
